label: Kevin D. Randle
narrative: Kevin Douglas Randle (born 4 June 1949) is the closest thing the retrieval literature has to an internal auditor with a security background. He flew UH-1s with the 116th and 187th Assault Helicopter Companies in Vietnam, served in the Air Force as a public affairs officer, general's aide and intelligence officer, completed Air Force Reserve service as a captain and director of intelligence for an airlift group, then joined the Iowa National Guard as an intelligence officer after 11 September 2001, deploying with the 234th Signal Battalion to Baghdad International Airport in June 2003 and retiring as a lieutenant colonel in 2009. With Donald R. Schmitt he wrote 'UFO Crash at Roswell' (1991) and 'The Truth About the UFO Crash at Roswell' (1994), the two books that drove Roswell into congressional attention and produced the Air Force counter-reports. Randle is important to this board precisely because he moved against the current: he demolished the Majestic 12 documents in 'Conclusions on Operation Majestic Twelve' (1994) and 'Case MJ-12' (2002) while Friedman defended them, he withdrew his and Schmitt's support for witnesses who did not hold up, and he later told Skeptical Inquirer's Robert Sheaffer that he sets a very high bar for evidence, that most abductees are describing sleep paralysis, and eventually that he was 'no longer sure what actually happened' at Roswell and that the case for extraterrestrial involvement 'is no longer robust.' He also wrote 'Project Moon Dust' (1999), 'A History of UFO Crashes' (1995) and 'Crash: When UFOs Fall From the Sky' (2010), which is the field's most systematic case-by-case survey.
